prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Desktop Pet Control Guide Screen [finish, new_screen]: predicted +10.0%, measured -11.2% ± 4.6%, after noise correction -3.5%, lost: worse
- round 2: Pet Selection Grid Redesign [adoption, redesign]: predicted +6.0%, measured -3.2% ± 3.9%, after noise correction -1.3%, lost: no clear effect

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- adoption, redesign: -1.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: -3.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Previous lessons:
The evidence is still thin to establish rules, as only one test has been completed so far.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Evidence is still thin to establish rules for specific kinds of changes, as no change type has been tested at least twice.
Predictions were consistently too high in both tests conducted so far.
